selection_rule: FREEZE ADDENDUM 3 decomposition pass: 2 components per MIXED parent (candidate-real + surface) authored by a sealed frontier decomposer, plus FREEZE ADDENDUM 4 position-fingerprint channels; every component is routed INDEPENDENTLY by the blind audit

selected.name: Recallable formulation judged independent of length or typography
selected.instruction: Read the contest prompt and the entry together. Ask only this: does the entry contain a formulation - a verbal image, a coinage, an unexpected pairing of words, a compressed comparison - that a reader could reproduce from memory after a single reading? Judge the formulation itself in the context of the prompt, not how the text is presented. You must NOT reward, at all, any of the following: how many characters the entry has, how many words are capitalised, how tidy or complete the typography is, how many punctuation marks appear, or how elaborate the sentence construction is. Score 10 when there is a sharp, distinctive formulation that would survive being retold in someone else's words with the same wording kept intact - this can and often will be a very short, all-lowercase, unpunctuated entry. Score 5 when a phrase is clear and coherent but ordinary, the kind of wording many entrants would produce. Score 0 when the wording is cumbersome, incoherent, or purely generic, with nothing a reader would carry away - a long, heavily punctuated, immaculately typed entry with no distinctive formulation must score 0. If the entry contains no substantive authored phrase at all, score 0.
selected.rationale: The parent named a craft property (compression into a retainable phrase) but its judged score can rise on typographic bulk and capitalised emphasis, which make text look emphatic and quotable. This version forces the judge to name the retained formulation and bans the carrier explicitly. Two-way dissociation: an entry of four plain lowercase words with a startling coined pairing scores 10 here while scoring at the bottom of the surface channel; a maximum-length entry with several SHOUTED words, full punctuation and correct capitalisation but only stock phrasing scores 0 here while topping the surface channel.
member_names: Recallable formulation judged independent of length or typography

selected.name: Extent of text bulk and capitalised emphasis
selected.instruction: This is a counting task, not an evaluation. Estimate from the text alone the combined magnitude of two mechanical quantities: (a) total length in characters, and (b) the proportion of letters that are uppercase, including fully capitalised words used for emphasis and capitalised sentence starts. Score 0 when the entry is very short (roughly under 40 characters) and essentially all lowercase. Score 5 for a mid-length entry (roughly 80-120 characters) with ordinary sentence-case capitalisation. Score 10 when the entry runs near the full tweet length AND carries heavy uppercase - multiple all-caps words or a largely capitalised line. Interpolate for intermediate cases. You must NOT decide whether this length or capitalisation is good, appropriate, funny, or well judged, and you must not let the content of the entry move the number. Report extent only.
selected.rationale: Character count and uppercase ratio are the mechanical carriers the interaction screen flagged for this parent: they make a line look emphatic and thus quotable to a judge without any compression actually occurring. Two-way dissociation: a maximum-length all-caps entry of pure cliche scores 10 here and 0 on D01; a six-word lowercase coinage scores near 0 here and 10 on D01.
member_names: Extent of text bulk and capitalised emphasis
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Memorable compact image or phrase

selected.name: Observational accuracy about a real shared behaviour
selected.instruction: Read the contest prompt and the entry together. Ask only this: does the entry isolate a behaviour, frustration, social rule, or lived experience with enough precision that a reader who has lived it would recognise it as accurate? Judge the accuracy and specificity of the observation in the context of the prompt. You must NOT reward, at all: length, number of capitalised or all-caps words, number of hashtags, punctuation volume, or neatness of typing. Emphatic styling is not evidence that an observation is true; plain typing is not evidence that it is false. Score 10 for a precise, specific observation that names a real detail of the behaviour rather than gesturing at the category - a short lowercase fragment naming one exact telling detail belongs at 10. Score 5 for a broad commonplace that is true but unspecific. Score 0 when the entry makes an observational claim that rings false, is internally inconsistent, or is so vague that no recognisable behaviour is picked out - including a long, hashtag-laden, heavily capitalised entry that only asserts a mood. If the entry makes no observational claim at all, score 0.
selected.rationale: The parent measures fidelity of observation, but judged fidelity can ride on emphatic capitalisation, bulk, and hashtag padding, all of which read as confident assertion. This version anchors the score to the presence of a specific, checkable behavioural detail. Two-way dissociation: a plain seven-word lowercase line naming an exact domestic detail scores 10 here and near 0 on D04; a long entry with three hashtags and shouted words asserting a vague grievance scores 0 here and 10 on D04.
member_names: Observational accuracy about a real shared behaviour

selected.name: Extent of capitals, length, and hashtag count
selected.instruction: This is a counting task, not an evaluation. Estimate from the text alone the combined magnitude of three mechanical quantities: (a) the proportion of letters that are uppercase, (b) total character length, and (c) the number of hashtag tokens (any token beginning with #, including the contest hashtag and any extras). Score 0 for a short, all-lowercase entry with at most the single contest hashtag or none. Score 5 for a mid-length entry with sentence-case capitalisation and one or two hashtags. Score 10 for a long entry with heavy uppercase and three or more hashtags. Interpolate for intermediate cases. You must NOT decide whether the capitalisation, length, or hashtag use is good, appropriate, spammy, or well judged. Report extent only.
selected.rationale: These are the exact mechanical features the interaction screen paired with this parent; hashtag stacking and capitalisation are habits that travel with assertive-sounding entries without adding observational precision. Two-way dissociation: an entry that is three stacked hashtags plus a shouted generic complaint scores 10 here and 0 on D03; a bare lowercase sentence with one precise observed detail scores 0-1 here and 10 on D03.
member_names: Extent of capitals, length, and hashtag count
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Observation has recognizable truth

selected.name: Distance of the angle from the prompt's stock associations
selected.instruction: Read the contest prompt first and privately list the two or three associations that come to mind immediately from the prompt alone. Then read the entry and ask only this: how far is the entry's angle of attack from that stock list? Judge the choice of connection, target, or viewpoint in context. You must NOT reward, at all: length, complexity of sentence construction, long or unusual words used for their own sake, capitalisation, or punctuation volume. Elaborate phrasing of an obvious idea is still an obvious idea. Score 10 when the entry reaches the prompt through a connection you did not list and would not have listed - a four-word plainly typed entry can score 10. Score 5 for a familiar idea carrying some individual twist. Score 0 for a near-restatement of the prompt, or a first stock association delivered straight, however long, ornate, or immaculately typed the delivery is. If the entry has too little content to locate any angle, score 0.
selected.rationale: Originality of angle is a craft property, but a judge can mistake syntactic elaboration and high readability-index texture for conceptual reach. Forcing the judge to pre-commit to the stock list makes the comparison about the idea rather than the prose surface. Two-way dissociation: a terse lowercase entry attacking the prompt from an unlisted direction scores 10 here and low on D06; a long, multi-clause, polysyllabic restatement of the prompt's most obvious reading scores 0 here and 10 on D06.
member_names: Distance of the angle from the prompt's stock associations

selected.name: Extent of length and long-word, long-clause complexity
selected.instruction: This is a counting task, not an evaluation. Estimate from the text alone the combined magnitude of three mechanical quantities: (a) total character length, (b) surface reading difficulty as a readability index would compute it - average word length in characters and average number of words per sentence, and (c) the proportion of uppercase letters. Score 0 for a short entry built from short common words in one brief clause, all lowercase. Score 5 for a mid-length entry of ordinary word length and one or two normal sentences. Score 10 for a long entry with conspicuously long words and long multi-clause sentences, plus heavy capitalisation. Interpolate for intermediate cases. You must NOT decide whether this complexity is good, apt, pretentious, or well judged, and the wit of the content must not move the number. Report extent only.
selected.rationale: Character count, uppercase ratio, and the automated readability index are the flagged carriers for this parent: verbal density reads as intellectual reach. Two-way dissociation: a long polysyllabic multi-clause paraphrase of the obvious take scores 10 here and 0 on D05; a blunt monosyllabic swerve scores 0 here and 10 on D05.
member_names: Extent of length and long-word, long-clause complexity
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Original angle within the prompt

selected.name: Speaker made legible by word choice, not styling
selected.instruction: Read the entry and ask only this: can you name a particular kind of speaker - an age, a role, a mood-state, a social position, a type of person - who would plausibly be the one saying this line, and is that inference driven by the entry's diction, idiom, and viewpoint? State the speaker to yourself before scoring. You must NOT treat any of these as evidence of voice: total length, all-caps or capitalisation choices, exclamation marks or punctuation volume, or neat versus messy typing. Shouting is not a character; tidy typography is not a character. Score 10 when a specific speaker is legible from word choice and stance alone and the whole line is consistent with that speaker - a short, plainly typed line using one telling idiom belongs at 10. Score 5 when only a generic attitude or unmarked everyperson is detectable. Score 0 when the voice is inconsistent across the line, or when no speaker beyond a neutral narrator can be inferred - including long, heavily capitalised, well-punctuated entries whose only apparent persona is loudness. If the line is deliberately impersonal, score 0.
selected.rationale: Implied voice is a diction property, but judged voice can be manufactured by shouting capitals and by long elaborated sentences that simulate a talker. Requiring the judge to name the speaker from diction isolates the craft. Two-way dissociation: a five-word lowercase line whose single regional or occupational idiom pins the speaker scores 10 here and near 0 on D08; a long ALL-CAPS rant in unmarked generic English scores 0 here and 10 on D08.
member_names: Speaker made legible by word choice, not styling

selected.name: Extent of shouted capitals and elaborated sentence length
selected.instruction: This is a counting task, not an evaluation. Estimate from the text alone the combined magnitude of three mechanical quantities: (a) the proportion of uppercase letters, counting fully capitalised words separately, (b) total character length, and (c) average words per sentence and average word length as a readability index would compute them. Score 0 for a short, all-lowercase entry of one brief clause. Score 5 for mid-length sentence-case text of ordinary construction. Score 10 for a long entry with multiple all-caps words or a mostly capitalised line and long multi-clause sentences. Interpolate for intermediate cases. You must NOT decide whether this styling is good, expressive, obnoxious, or well judged, and you must not let any impression of personality move the number. Report extent only.
selected.rationale: Uppercase ratio, length, and readability index are the flagged carriers here: capitals mimic vocal delivery and long constructions mimic a person talking, so a judge can read persona off pure formatting. Two-way dissociation given in D07 applies in both directions.
member_names: Extent of shouted capitals and elaborated sentence length
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Character voice is implied

selected.name: Specific comic attitude carried by word choice alone
selected.instruction: Read the entry and ask only this: does the wording convey one specific comic attitude - mock outrage, delight, embarrassment, resignation, smugness, dread, exhaustion, defiance - and does that attitude fit and support the idea being expressed? Name the attitude to yourself in one word before scoring, and check that you could still name it if the entry were retyped in plain lowercase with no exclamation marks. You must NOT reward: capitalisation, exclamation marks, elongated spellings, emoji-like emphasis, length, or sentence complexity. Score 10 when a single distinct attitude is unmistakable from diction and stance and it strengthens the idea - a short plain line whose one verb carries the whole attitude belongs at 10. Score 5 when the attitude is present but generic, or when two attitudes are mixed without control. Score 0 when the tone contradicts or undercuts the idea, when no attitude survives the plain-lowercase test, or when the only apparent attitude is volume - a long, heavily capitalised, exclamation-laden entry with no attitude legible in its word choice must score 0. If no attitude is expressed at all, score 0.
selected.rationale: Attitude is a diction and stance property, but judged attitude is easily faked by uppercase and emphatic typography; the plain-lowercase retyping test is the operational separator. Two-way dissociation: a flat lowercase seven-word line whose verb choice makes weary resignation unmistakable scores 10 here and near 0 on D10; a maximum-length entry of CAPS and repeated letters whose word choice conveys nothing specific scores 0 here and 10 on D10.
member_names: Specific comic attitude carried by word choice alone

selected.name: Extent of capitalised and elongated emphasis markers
selected.instruction: This is a counting task, not an evaluation. Estimate from the text alone the combined magnitude of three mechanical quantities: (a) the proportion of uppercase letters, including all-caps words, (b) total character length, and (c) surface reading difficulty as a readability index would compute it - average word length and average words per sentence. Count elongated spellings (repeated letters such as sooo) toward (a) as emphasis markers. Score 0 for a short all-lowercase entry with no emphasis markers. Score 5 for a mid-length sentence-case entry with at most one emphatic word. Score 10 for a long entry with several all-caps or elongated words. Interpolate for intermediate cases. You must NOT decide whether the emphasis is good, sincere, overdone, or well judged. Report extent only.
selected.rationale: Uppercase ratio, length, and readability index are the flagged carriers: emphasis typography is the cheapest possible signal of feeling and travels with, but is not, legible attitude. Two-way dissociation as stated in D09, in both directions.
member_names: Extent of capitalised and elongated emphasis markers
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Emotional attitude is legible

selected.name: Cadence functionally timed to the final beat
selected.instruction: Read the entry aloud in your head, then ask only this: is the arrangement of the words - clause lengths, parallel structures, repetition, sound echo, word order - doing work to place and time the line's last comic beat? The test is functional: would moving the final word or phrase earlier, or flattening the parallelism, measurably weaken the line? You must NOT reward: total length, number of clauses for their own sake, capitalisation, punctuation volume, or neat typography. A long entry can be rhythmically shapeless and a very short entry can be perfectly timed. Score 10 when the cadence is clearly functional - the last beat lands where the structure has prepared it - and a six-word lowercase entry with one deliberate reversal belongs at 10. Score 5 when some cadence is present but roughness or a stray clause blunts the landing. Score 0 when the arrangement obstructs the attempted line, buries the last beat mid-sentence, or is merely a run of clauses with no timing at all, however long and correctly punctuated. If no rhythmic structure is evident, score 0.
selected.rationale: Rhythm judgements drift toward simply counting clauses and admiring long tidy constructions; the functional test (would rearranging hurt it?) forces the judge to assess timing rather than bulk. Two-way dissociation: a short lowercase line with one parallel pair and a terminal reversal scores 10 here and near 0 on D12; a long, correctly capitalised, multi-clause entry whose payoff sits in the middle and whose clauses are all the same shape scores 0 here and 10 on D12.
member_names: Cadence functionally timed to the final beat

selected.name: Extent of clause count and sentence-length variation
selected.instruction: This is a counting task, not an evaluation. Estimate from the text alone the combined magnitude of three mechanical quantities: (a) total character length, (b) the number of clauses or sentence-like segments and their average word length as a readability index would compute it, and (c) the proportion of uppercase letters. Score 0 for a short single-clause all-lowercase entry. Score 5 for a mid-length entry of two clauses in sentence case. Score 10 for a long entry of three or more clauses with long words and heavy capitalisation. Interpolate for intermediate cases. You must NOT decide whether the structure is rhythmic, well timed, clumsy, or well judged. Count structure, do not hear it. Report extent only.
selected.rationale: Character count, readability index, and uppercase ratio are the flagged carriers: more clauses and longer words make text look composed and deliberate whether or not any timing exists. Two-way dissociation as stated in D11, in both directions.
member_names: Extent of clause count and sentence-length variation
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Rhythm supports the payoff

selected.name: Genuine redirection of an established expectation
selected.instruction: Read the entry and ask only this: does its wording first build a specific expectation and then supply a turn you did not anticipate, where the turn still makes sense in retrospect? Before scoring, state to yourself what the expectation was and what replaced it. You must NOT reward: length, the presence of a comma or dash before the ending, capitalisation, @-mentions, or punctuation volume. Setup and turn can be accomplished inside a handful of words with no punctuation at all. Score 10 when both halves are clear, the turn is genuinely non-obvious, and the ending re-reads the beginning - a very short, plainly typed entry belongs at 10 when it does this. Score 5 when a turn is present but you saw it coming from the setup. Score 0 when a setup is built and the turn is confusing, absent, or a mere continuation - including a long entry with tidy punctuation, mentions, and capitals that simply keeps going. If the entry has no setup-turn structure at all, score 0.
selected.rationale: The turn is a structural craft property, but a judge can read a long line with a punctuated tail and a tagged handle as if it had a punchline shape. Naming the expectation and the replacement forces the structural check. Two-way dissociation: a five-word lowercase line whose last word reframes the first three scores 10 here and near 0 on D14; a long capitalised entry with two @-mentions and a trailing clause that merely elaborates scores 0 here and 10 on D14.
member_names: Genuine redirection of an established expectation

selected.name: Extent of length, capitals, and mention count
selected.instruction: This is a counting task, not an evaluation. Estimate from the text alone the combined magnitude of three mechanical quantities: (a) total character length, (b) the proportion of uppercase letters including all-caps words, and (c) the number of @-mention tokens (any token beginning with @). Score 0 for a short all-lowercase entry with no mentions. Score 5 for a mid-length sentence-case entry with at most one mention. Score 10 for a long entry with heavy capitalisation and two or more mentions. Interpolate for intermediate cases. You must NOT decide whether the length, capitalisation, or tagging is good, appropriate, spammy, or well judged. Report extent only.
selected.rationale: Character count, uppercase ratio, and mention count are the flagged carriers for this parent; mentions and bulk lengthen a line so that its ending arrives late and reads as a tail even when nothing is redirected. Two-way dissociation as stated in D13, in both directions.
member_names: Extent of length, capitals, and mention count
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Surprising turn

selected.name: New meaning created by the alteration
selected.instruction: Identify the source the entry is playing on (a title, lyric, saying, brand, catchphrase, or the prompt's own template) and the alteration made to it. Then ask only this: does the alteration produce a NEW meaning that answers the prompt, rather than merely resembling the source or swapping one word for a similar-sounding one to no end? State the old meaning and the new meaning to yourself before scoring. You must NOT reward: length, number of @-mentions, capitalisation of titles or brand names, punctuation volume, or how faithfully the source is typed out. Score 10 when the changed element carries a clear new meaning that lands against the prompt - a one-word substitution in a short lowercase line belongs at 10 when the substitution does real semantic work. Score 5 when the change is mostly cosmetic, a near-homophone, or only weakly relevant to the prompt. Score 0 when the alteration yields no coherent new meaning - including a long, immaculately capitalised entry that quotes a source at length and changes one incidental word. If no source is transformed, score 0.
selected.rationale: The craft here is semantic (does the change mean something new?), but quoting a source at length and capitalising it properly makes an entry look like a well-executed parody. Requiring the old-meaning/new-meaning statement isolates the semantics. Two-way dissociation: a short lowercase line with one meaning-bearing substitution scores 10 here and near 0 on D16; a long entry reproducing a title in full caps with two tagged handles and a cosmetic tweak scores 0 here and 10 on D16.
member_names: New meaning created by the alteration

selected.name: Extent of length, mention count, and capitals
selected.instruction: This is a counting task, not an evaluation. Estimate from the text alone the combined magnitude of three mechanical quantities: (a) total character length, (b) the number of @-mention tokens, and (c) the proportion of uppercase letters, including title-case or all-caps rendering of names and quoted sources. Score 0 for a short all-lowercase entry with no mentions. Score 5 for a mid-length entry with ordinary capitalisation and at most one mention. Score 10 for a long entry with two or more mentions and heavy or title-case capitalisation throughout. Interpolate for intermediate cases. You must NOT decide whether the quoting, tagging, or capitalisation is good, accurate, or well judged. Report extent only.
selected.rationale: Character count, mention count, and uppercase ratio are the flagged carriers: reproducing a source verbatim inflates all three and signals parody competence without any meaning being changed. Two-way dissociation as stated in D15, in both directions.
member_names: Extent of length, mention count, and capitals
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Transformation changes the meaning

selected.name: Every word load-bearing for the comic idea
selected.instruction: Read the entry and ask only this: what proportion of the authored words are doing work for the comic idea? Try deleting words: greetings, address to the contest or host, pleading or self-commentary, restatement of the prompt, duplicated hashtags, throat-clearing preambles, and explanation of the joke after it has landed. Judge on the density of necessary words, NOT on the raw amount of text. A long entry in which every clause is load-bearing must be able to score 10, and a very short entry that is mostly a greeting or a bare restatement must be able to score 0. You must NOT reward or penalise: total length as such, capitalisation, punctuation volume, or @-mentions except insofar as a mention is itself removable filler. Score 10 when nearly nothing can be deleted without losing the idea. Score 5 when minor trimming would help but nothing materially delays the idea. Score 0 when removable material materially delays or obscures the idea, or when the entry is mostly filler with a fragment of an idea attached. If there is no substantive authored content, score 0.
selected.rationale: Economy is a ratio (needed words over total words) but the judged version collapses toward the denominator alone, so short entries are read as economical and long ones as padded regardless of content. Framing it as a deletion test restores the ratio. Two-way dissociation: a maximum-length entry in which every clause is required scores 10 here and 10 on D18 - so the pair is checked in the other direction too: a very short entry reading hey guys please RT #contest scores 0 here and near 0 on D18, while a long fully load-bearing entry scores 10 here and 10 on D18. The genuinely separating cases are these two: long-and-necessary (10 here, high on D18) and short-and-filler (0 here, low on D18), which run the two channels in opposite directions relative to each other.
member_names: Every word load-bearing for the comic idea

selected.name: Extent of overall length, mentions, and capitals
selected.instruction: This is a counting task, not an evaluation. Estimate from the text alone the combined magnitude of three mechanical quantities: (a) total character length, (b) the number of @-mention tokens, and (c) the proportion of uppercase letters. Score 0 for a very short all-lowercase entry with no mentions. Score 5 for a mid-length sentence-case entry with at most one mention. Score 10 for an entry at or near the full tweet length with two or more mentions and heavy capitalisation. Interpolate for intermediate cases. You must NOT decide whether the entry is padded, concise, cluttered, efficient, or well judged - brevity is not virtue here and length is not vice. Report extent only.
selected.rationale: Character count, mention count and uppercase ratio are the flagged carriers, and for this parent the carrier is nearly a proxy for the parent itself, which is exactly why it must be split off. Two-way dissociation: a long entry with every word load-bearing scores 10 on D17 and 9-10 here; a short greeting-plus-hashtag entry scores 0 on D17 and 0-1 here - the two channels therefore disagree sharply on precisely the cases where economy and brevity come apart, which is what the split is for.
member_names: Extent of overall length, mentions, and capitals
selected.upstream_parent: surface carrier of bank criterion: Economical wording

selected.name: Reads as a first, most obvious reading of the prompt
selected.instruction: Read the contest prompt, then the entry. Estimate the extent to which the entry takes the single most immediately available reading of the prompt - the association almost anyone would reach for in the first few seconds, the most literal template fill, or a near-restatement of the prompt with one slot filled. Score 10 when the entry occupies exactly that first-reading slot with no detour. Score 5 when it starts from an available reading but moves one step off it. Score 0 when the entry's route into the prompt is one that only turns up after the obvious readings are already exhausted - an oblique target, a second-order reading, or an angle that presupposes the direct ones have been taken. This is NOT a quality judgement: obvious entries are not being marked down and oblique entries are not being marked up; you are estimating position on an obvious-to-oblique axis only. Do not consider length, capitalisation, or typography.
selected.rationale: Entrants arriving early face an unpicked prompt and take the near associations; entrants arriving later can see that the obvious takes are gone and must go further out, so obviousness is a textual fingerprint of arrival order and of how crowded the container already was. It is marked mixed because distance from stock associations is also part of what the originality criterion tries to measure - the channel cannot be assumed to be positional alone, and its overlap with D05 must be treated as real.
selected.upstream_parent: How early the entry was written relative to its sibling entries in the same contest
member_names: Reads as a first, most obvious reading of the prompt

selected.name: Presupposes a shared running joke or prior entries
selected.instruction: Estimate the extent to which the entry only fully parses if the reader already shares something the entry does not supply: a running gag in this contest or hashtag community, a callback to a joke someone else is assumed to have made, an in-group referent introduced elsewhere, or a phrase used as though it were already established. Score 10 when the entry is unreadable as a standalone line without that assumed shared material - it behaves like a reply to a conversation in progress. Score 5 when there is a light gesture toward shared context but the line still stands alone. Score 0 when the entry is fully self-contained and needs only the prompt. This is NOT a quality judgement: neither self-contained nor context-dependent entries are better; estimate dependence on assumed shared material only.
selected.rationale: Presupposing a shared running joke is only possible once a container has accumulated enough material to run, so it fingerprints lateness and crowding. It is marked mixed because callback construction is also a comic craft move, so the channel may carry construct content as well as position; it must not be read as a pure positional instrument.
selected.upstream_parent: How late the entry sits in the container, and how many sibling entries preceded it
member_names: Presupposes a shared running joke or prior entries

selected.name: Vocabulary pins the entry to a specific moment in time
selected.instruction: Estimate the extent to which the entry's vocabulary, referents, or idiom fix it to a particular period or news moment: a named person or event current only briefly, a platform feature or product of a specific era, a slang term with a datable lifespan, a price or technology marker. Score 10 when a reader could name the month or season from the wording alone. Score 5 when the wording narrows it to a broad era of a few years. Score 0 when nothing in the wording dates the entry - it could have been written at any point in the contest's history. This is NOT a quality judgement: topicality is neither a merit nor a fault here. Estimate datedness of the vocabulary only.
selected.rationale: Datable vocabulary indexes when the container ran, not how good the entry is; two entries of identical craft written years apart differ on this channel purely by their containers' calendar position. It is not mixed because nothing in the construct - how good the tweet is as a contest entry - is defined by whether its referents are datable.
selected.upstream_parent: Where this contest falls in the long run of contests (calendar position of the container)
member_names: Vocabulary pins the entry to a specific moment in time

selected.name: Marks itself as an addition to an existing pile
selected.instruction: Estimate the extent to which the entry explicitly signals that it is one of many - phrasing such as another one, also, and again, part two, ok last one, one more, plus continuation markers, numbering, or a construction that reads as appended to a series the author or the crowd is already producing. Score 10 when the entry openly announces itself as an additional item in a series. Score 5 when there is a mild continuation marker (an opening also or and) but no explicit series framing. Score 0 when the entry is framed as a standalone first statement with no continuation signal. This is NOT a quality judgement: series markers are neither good nor bad. Count and estimate the signalling only.
selected.rationale: Self-marking as an addition is a direct textual trace of submitting into an already-populated container and of the author's own submission depth - both pure position facts. It is not mixed because the construct concerns the comic quality of the line, and a continuation marker is orthogonal to that; if anything it is removable filler, which the economy component already handles separately.
selected.upstream_parent: How many entries already exist in the container, and how many the same author has already submitted
member_names: Marks itself as an addition to an existing pile

selected.name: Uses contest-community conventions, formats, or meta-references
selected.instruction: Estimate the extent to which the entry deploys conventions specific to this hashtag-game community rather than general tweet writing: the game's standard template or set-up-then-answer format, meta-reference to the contest, the host, or the hashtag round itself, community-standard abbreviations or tagging habits, or a formatting convention recognisable as this game's house style. Score 10 when the entry is built entirely from house conventions a newcomer would not know. Score 5 when one convention is used but the rest is general-purpose writing. Score 0 when nothing in the entry reflects any convention particular to this contest community. This is NOT a quality judgement: convention use is neither skilful nor unskilful here. Estimate the density of community-specific convention only.
selected.rationale: House conventions accumulate over the life of a recurring contest, so convention density fingerprints both the container's position in the series and the author's tenure - facts about where the entry sits, not about the line's comic merit. It is marked not mixed because the construct is defined over the tweet as a comic entry, and fluency in a formatting convention can be present in weak entries and absent in strong ones.
selected.upstream_parent: How deep into the long run of contests the container sits, and how established the author is within it
member_names: Uses contest-community conventions, formats, or meta-references
